name: Boyzone
notes: The 1990s Irish ballad template Westlife inherited, and Gate-2 clear at 1994. The research gives 70–100 with a half-time ballad feel and the backbeat on 3, so `halfTime` is true and the snare is `halftime_3`. Its drum grammar is distinct from the Westlife entry in three named ways and those are the deltas: "tambourine 8ths from chorus 1" (a tambourine-led perc block at a higher density), "brush-swept fills" (a soft velocity tier with a low ramp on the snare roll), and "almost no hat above 8ths" — a pinned 8th base with the fill density lower than anything else in the section. Harmony is the stated I–iii–IV–V and I–V–vi–IV with an occasional final-chorus semitone lift, and the melody is written from "solo lead voice for a full verse before harmony enters; melody in a 9th-span, chorus written around a repeated title hook on beats 1–2" — a narrow register, a low density and a two-bar phrase. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research says so and marks the tempo **[LOW-CONF]**: only two catalogue readings exist, 77 and 96, so the 70–100 window is the research's and `bpm.mode` 84 is this author's midpoint between the two readings. ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are all drum probabilities; the entry says the drum grammar is largely convention-based and this model does not pretend otherwise. ⛔ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than `reese_sustain`, and that is an engine limit rather than a reading of the record.** `reese_sustain` is the only rhythm `bass.rs` reads that holds a note, and it emits one note per chord — TASK-162, still open — so this model measured **256 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** on it against `bass.rs`'s floor of 500. `mirror_kick` with a high root lock is the roster-wide substitution for a sustained sub (`dmx`, `coolio`, `krs-one`, `mobb-deep` all record the same one), and over a kick that plays 1 and 3 with a `2&` pickup it reads as held at this tempo. The research is *"sustained keyboard bass roots, plus fretless-style slides between chord changes on the ballads"* — the slides are `glideProb` 0.28, which is untouched, and the roots are `followRootsProb`. ⚠ **INFERRED:** `followRootsProb` 0.92 and `anticipationProb` 0.16 are lane-conventional values for a ballad keyboard bass, not sourced ones — the research names no rate for either. They are what lets the part reach a producer's 500 basslines; 0.95/0.10 was the authored pair and it reached 256.
